title: Climate Analog Search Tools
text: analogs package provides fast, flexible tools climate analog analyses. efficiently searches large reference datasets find locations best match query sites based climate similarity geographic proximity.

title: Climate Analog Search Tools
text: package supports range analyses. fully customized queries, can call core analog_search() function. Common query types supported via dedicated helper functions: analog_velocity() finds k nearest geographic analogs hard climate constraint analog_impact() finds k nearest climate analogs within geographic constraint analog_availability() counts analogs meet climate distance thresholds analog_intensity() computes distance-weighted aggregations analog properties Geographic distance computations support projected coordinates well lon-lat coordinates via great circle distances. Multivariate climate distances Euclidean default, can use mahalanobis_transform() implement Mahalanobis distance based global spatial covariance, supply x_cov analog_*() function account site-specific climate covariance patterns.

title: Climate Analog Search Tools
text: analogs uses optimized C++ algorithms parallel processing handle computationally intensive pairwise distance calculations across millions locations. package built around lattice search index. functions sufficient many analyses, optimization possible using build_analog_index() pre-build reusable search index, using tune_index_res() find optimal index parameters specific data.

title: Analog intensity: weighted sum of analogs within climate/geographic limits — analog_intensity
text: x Focal locations analogs found. matrix/data.frame columns x, y, climate variables, SpatRaster climate variable layers. pool reference dataset search analogs. Either: Matrix/data.frame columns x, y, climate variables,     SpatRaster climate variable layers, analog_index object created     build_analog_index (repeated queries). max_clim Maximum climate distance constraint (default: NULL = climate constraint). Can either: scalar: Euclidean radius climate space (e.g., 0.5) vector: Per-variable absolute differences (length must equal     number climate variables) reference locations within climate distance considered. x_cov provided, scalar thresholds interpreted Mahalanobis distance units. max_geog Maximum geographic distance constraint (default: NULL = geographic constraint). specified, reference locations within distance considered. Radius units specified kilometers coord_type = "lonlat", projected coordinate units coord_type = "projected". weight Weighting function matches, used aggregate "sum_weights" "mean_weights". One : "uniform": matches weighted equally (weight = 1.0). "inverse_clim": Inverse climate distance,     weight = 1 / (climate_distance + eps), epsilon given theta. "inverse_geog": Inverse geographic distance,     weight = 1 / (geographic_distance + eps), epsilon given theta. "gaussian_clim": Gaussian kernel climate distance,     weight = exp(-climate_distance^2 / (2*sigma^2)), sigma given theta. "gaussian_geog": Gaussian kernel geographic distance,     weight = exp(-geographic_distance^2 / (2*sigma^2)), sigma given theta. "gaussian_joint": Joint Gaussian kernel,     weight = exp(-climate_distance^2/(2*sigma_c^2) - geographic_distance^2/(2*sigma_g^2)),     sigma values given theta 2-element vector c(sigma_clim, sigma_geog). "inverse_joint": Joint inverse distance,     weight = 1 / sqrt((climate_distance + eps_clim)^2 + (geographic_distance + eps_geog)^2),     epsilon values given theta 2-element vector c(eps_clim, eps_geog). aggregate NULL, "pairs", "count", weight must NULL. theta Optional numeric parameter used weighting functions aggregate "sum_weights" "mean_weights" weight "uniform". Interpretation depends weight: "inverse_clim" "inverse_geog": epsilon value     added distances (scalar; default: 1e-12 climate, 1e-6 geography). "gaussian_clim" "gaussian_geog": sigma bandwidth     parameter (scalar; larger values = slower decay distance). "gaussian_joint": 2-element vector c(sigma_clim, sigma_geog)     giving bandwidths climate geographic dimensions. "inverse_joint": 2-element vector c(eps_clim, eps_geog)     giving epsilon values climate geographic dimensions. theta NULL, sensible defaults used single-parameter weights. weight = "uniform" non-weighted aggregations, theta must NULL. x_cov Optional focal-specific covariance matrices Mahalanobis distance calculations. matrix data.frame one row per focal location one column per unique covariance component. n climate variables, n*(n+1)/2 unique components, ordered : variances first (diagonals), covariances (upper triangle row). coord_type Coordinate system type (default: "auto"): "auto": Automatically detect coordinate ranges. "lonlat": Unprojected lon/lat coordinates (uses great-circle distance;     assumes max_geog km). "projected": Projected XY coordinates (uses planar distance;     assumes max_geog projection units). index_res Tuning parameter giving number bins per dimension internally-used lattice search index. Either: positive integer. "auto" (default): Automatically tune index resolution     optimizing compute time subsample focal points. focal     relatively rows, auto-tuning skipped default resolution     16 used. Ignored pool analog_index (uses index's resolution). n_threads Optional integer number threads use computation. NULL (default), global RcppParallel setting used (see RcppParallel::setThreadOptions).

title: Build Analog Index — build_analog_index
text: lattice index built geographic climate dimensions, allowing efficient spatial queries regardless constraint values used query time. lon/lat coordinates, index uses ECEF (Earth-Centered Earth-Fixed) space internally optimal performance. Index resolution (index_res) controls granularity spatial binning. optimal value depends data size query patterns. Use tune_index_res find best resolution use case, accept default 16 works well applications.

Must number climate variables x. format options x. center Logical; TRUE (default), center variable mean zero transformation. scale Logical; TRUE (default), standardize variable unit variance transformation (correlation-based). title: Tune Index Resolution — tune_index_res
code: tune_index_res(   x,   pool,   select = "all",   aggregate = NULL,   max_clim = NULL,   max_geog = NULL,   k = NULL,   weight = NULL,   theta = NULL,   x_cov = NULL,   coord_type = c("auto", "lonlat", "projected"),   n_threads = NULL,   default_res = 16L,   verbose = FALSE )

title: Tune Index Resolution — tune_index_res
text: x Focal locations analogs found. matrix/data.frame columns x, y, climate variables, SpatRaster climate variable layers. pool reference dataset search analogs. Either: Matrix/data.frame columns x, y, climate variables,     SpatRaster climate variable layers, analog_index object created     build_analog_index (repeated queries). select Character string specifying analog selection strategy. One : "" (default): Select analogs satisfy     max_clim max_geog constraints. "knn_clim": focal, select k analogs     smallest climate distance, subject filters. "knn_geog": focal, select k analogs     smallest geographic distance, subject filters. aggregate aggregate selected analogs. Either: NULL "pairs" (default): Return selected     analog pairs data.frame. "count": focal, count number selected analogs. "sum_weights": focal, sum weights selected     analogs (see weight theta). "mean_weights": focal, mean weights selected     analogs. max_clim Maximum climate distance constraint (default: NULL = climate constraint). Can either: scalar: Euclidean radius climate space (e.g., 0.5) vector: Per-variable absolute differences (length must equal     number climate variables) reference locations within climate distance considered. x_cov provided, scalar thresholds interpreted Mahalanobis distance units. max_geog Maximum geographic distance constraint (default: NULL = geographic constraint). specified, reference locations within distance considered. Radius units specified kilometers coord_type = "lonlat", projected coordinate units coord_type = "projected". k Number nearest analogs return per focal location kNN selection modes. Required select "knn_geog" "knn_clim"; must NULL select = "". weight Weighting function matches, used aggregate "sum_weights" "mean_weights". One : "uniform": matches weighted equally (weight = 1.0). "inverse_clim": Inverse climate distance,     weight = 1 / (climate_distance + eps), epsilon given theta. "inverse_geog": Inverse geographic distance,     weight = 1 / (geographic_distance + eps), epsilon given theta. "gaussian_clim": Gaussian kernel climate distance,     weight = exp(-climate_distance^2 / (2*sigma^2)), sigma given theta. "gaussian_geog": Gaussian kernel geographic distance,     weight = exp(-geographic_distance^2 / (2*sigma^2)), sigma given theta. "gaussian_joint": Joint Gaussian kernel,     weight = exp(-climate_distance^2/(2*sigma_c^2) - geographic_distance^2/(2*sigma_g^2)),     sigma values given theta 2-element vector c(sigma_clim, sigma_geog). "inverse_joint": Joint inverse distance,     weight = 1 / sqrt((climate_distance + eps_clim)^2 + (geographic_distance + eps_geog)^2),     epsilon values given theta 2-element vector c(eps_clim, eps_geog). aggregate NULL, "pairs", "count", weight must NULL. theta Optional numeric parameter used weighting functions aggregate "sum_weights" "mean_weights" weight "uniform". Interpretation depends weight: "inverse_clim" "inverse_geog": epsilon value     added distances (scalar; default: 1e-12 climate, 1e-6 geography). "gaussian_clim" "gaussian_geog": sigma bandwidth     parameter (scalar; larger values = slower decay distance). "gaussian_joint": 2-element vector c(sigma_clim, sigma_geog)     giving bandwidths climate geographic dimensions. "inverse_joint": 2-element vector c(eps_clim, eps_geog)     giving epsilon values climate geographic dimensions. theta NULL, sensible defaults used single-parameter weights. weight = "uniform" non-weighted aggregations, theta must NULL. x_cov Optional focal-specific covariance matrices Mahalanobis distance calculations. matrix data.frame one row per focal location one column per unique covariance component. n climate variables, n*(n+1)/2 unique components, ordered : variances first (diagonals), covariances (upper triangle row). coord_type Coordinate system type (default: "auto"): "auto": Automatically detect coordinate ranges. "lonlat": Unprojected lon/lat coordinates (uses great-circle distance;     assumes max_geog km). "projected": Projected XY coordinates (uses planar distance;     assumes max_geog projection units). n_threads Optional integer number threads use computation. NULL (default), global RcppParallel setting used (see RcppParallel::setThreadOptions). default_res Default resolution use starting point search. Default 16. verbose Logical; TRUE, print selected resolution. Default FALSE.

title: Tune Index Resolution — tune_index_res
text: integer giving recommended index resolution (bins per dimension).

title: Tune Index Resolution — tune_index_res
text: function uses adaptive bracketing algorithm: Starts three resolutions: default/2, default, default*2 Evaluates elapsed time minimum edge, expands search direction Returns resolution lowest elapsed time typically requires 3-5 query evaluations total, making much faster exhaustive grid search. function performs tuning non-trivial problem sizes (>2000 focal points). smaller datasets, returns default resolution. subsample focal points used benchmarking keep tuning fast still representative actual query performance.

title: Tune Index Resolution — tune_index_res
